                                      Full assumptions and notation

                                      All objects and hypotheses

                                      • E is finite-dimensional real Hilbert with Borel structure; H is a complete real inner-product normed space, with no separability assumption.
                                      • F:E→H has actual full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w. M1,M2≥0 bound the derivative operator norm and its operator Lipschitz increment on the closed unit ball.
                                      • y is fixed. S is the literal unit-norm subtype; m is the actual Bochner integral, c the literal arccos cost, and Q the infimum of angular squared cost over all actual couplings.

                                      Mathematical proof

                                      Open a step to read its argument and formula.

                                      1. Produce feature continuity and chord control

                                      Differentiability gives continuity. The convex mean-value bound on the closed unit ball produces the M1 chord Lipschitz estimate. Continuity on a second-countable domain yields strong measurability of the feature restriction even when H is not separable.

                                      \[\|F(w)-F(u)\|\le M_1\|w-u\|\quad(\|w\|,\|u\|\le1).\]
                                      Corresponding Lean step
                                        have hFc : Continuous F := continuous_iff_continuousAt.mpr fun w => (hF w).continuousAt
  have hKsm : StronglyMeasurable K := (hFc.comp continuous_subtype_val).stronglyMeasurable
  have hChord (w u : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) :
      ‖F w-F u‖ ≤ M₁*‖w-u‖ := by
    apply (convex_closedBall (0 : E) 1).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le
      (fun z _ => (hF z).hasFDerivWithinAt) ?_
      (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hu)
      (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hw)
    intro z hz
    exact hBound z (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hz)

                                      Literal module excerpt. Local names retain the surrounding theorem context, available with the complete folded theorem; these are proof ingredients, not extra public premises.

                                      2. Produce one uniform feature bound

                                      Compare every unit feature with F(0), using the previous estimate and the norm triangle inequality. The extra one makes B a convenient positive budget. This budget is an internal consequence, not a new premise.

                                      \[B=\|F(0)\|+M_1+1,\qquad\|F(w)\|\le B\quad(w\in S).\]
                                      Corresponding Lean step
                                        let B := ‖F (0:E)‖+M₁+1
  have hB : 0 ≤ B := by dsimp [B]; positivity
  have hKb (w : S) : ‖K w‖ ≤ B := by
    have hb := hChord w.1 0 w.property.le (by simp)
    have hn := norm_add_le (F w.1-F 0) (F 0)
    rw [sub_add_cancel] at hn
    simp only [sub_zero,w.property,mul_one] at hb
    change ‖F w.1‖ ≤ B
    dsimp [B]
    linarith

                                      Literal module excerpt. Local names retain the surrounding theorem context, available with the complete folded theorem; these are proof ingredients, not extra public premises.

                                      3. Pass from chords to angular cost

                                      The canonical angular-geometry result supplies measurability, nonnegativity, the pi upper bound and chord domination. Consequently K is M1 Lipschitz with respect to the actual angular cost.

                                      \[\|K(w)-K(u)\|\le M_1c(w,u),\qquad 0\le c(w,u)\le\pi.\]
                                      Corresponding Lean step
                                        have hAng := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost.unit_sphere_angular_cost_properties (E := E)
  change Continuous c ∧ Measurable c ∧
    (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧
      c (u,v) = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 ∧ ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ c (u,v) ∧
      (c (u,v) = 0 ↔ u = v) ∧ c (u,v) = c (v,u)) ∧
    ∀ u v w : S, c (u,w) ≤ c (u,v)+c (v,w) at hAng
  have hc0 (z : S × S) : 0 ≤ c z := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).1
  have hcB (z : S × S) : c z ≤ Real.pi := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).2.1
  have hKlip (w u : S) : ‖K w-K u‖ ≤ M₁*c (w,u) :=
    (hChord w.1 u.1 w.property.le u.property.le).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hAng.2.2.1 w u).2.2.2.1 hM₁)

                                      Literal module excerpt. Local names retain the surrounding theorem context, available with the complete folded theorem; these are proof ingredients, not extra public premises.

                                      4. Control actual means over all couplings

                                      Apply bounded Bochner transport to actual probability laws, not chosen optimal couplings. It produces integrability, finite Q, the mean difference estimate and the residual budget R0=B+norm(y).

                                      \[\|m_\mu-m_\nu\|\le M_1\sqrt{Q(\mu,\nu)},\qquad\|m_\mu-y\|\le R_0.\]
                                      Corresponding Lean step
                                        have hMean (μ ν : Measure S) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν] :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.BochnerMeanTransport.bounded_bochner_mean_quadratic_transport_control
      K hKsm B Real.pi M₁ hB Real.pi_pos.le hM₁ hKb c hAng.2.1 hc0 hcB hKlip μ ν
  have hTangent :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.QuadraticFeatureTangentGradient.quadratic_feature_potential_tangent_gradient
      F D hF M₁ M₂ hM₁ hM₂ hBound hLip
  let R₀ := B+‖y‖
  have hR₀ : 0 ≤ R₀ := add_nonneg hB (norm_nonneg y)
  have hResidual (μ : Measure S) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : ‖m μ-y‖ ≤ R₀ :=
    ((hMean μ μ).2.2.2.2 y).1

                                      Literal module excerpt. Local names retain the surrounding theorem context, available with the complete folded theorem; these are proof ingredients, not extra public premises.

                                      5. Identify the full ambient gradient

                                      For fixed residual r=m_mu-y the canonical scalar-potential derivative is 2 inner(D(w)*r,·). The real Riesz identification turns it into HasGradientAt, at every ambient weight rather than only unit points.

                                      \[\nabla V_\mu(w)=2D(w)^*(m_\mu-y).\]
                                      Corresponding Lean step
                                        have hGrad (μ : Measure S) (w : E) :
      HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) w := by
    rw [hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt]
    have he : InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) =
        (2 : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ ((D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) := by
      ext v
      simp [InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply,innerSL_apply_apply]
    rw [he]
    exact hTangent.1 (m μ-y) w

                                      Literal module excerpt. Local names retain the surrounding theorem context, available with the complete folded theorem; these are proof ingredients, not extra public premises.

                                      6. Choose constants before the laws

                                      Projection contraction gives the pointwise bound, while R0 is independent of the parameter law. Choose strictly positive C1,C2 before quantifying over all laws and weights. The constants are not claimed dimension free.

                                      \[C_1=2M_1R_0+1,\quad C_2=2M_1^2+2(M_2+2M_1)R_0+1.\]
                                      Corresponding Lean step
                                        let A := 2*M₁^2
  let B₂ := 2*(M₂+2*M₁)*R₀
  have hA : 0 ≤ A := by dsimp [A]; positivity
  have hB₂ : 0 ≤ B₂ := by dsimp [B₂]; positivity
  refine ⟨2*M₁*R₀+1,A+B₂+1,by positivity,by positivity,?_,?_⟩
  · intro μ hμ
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
    refine ⟨(hMean μ μ).1,hGrad μ,?_⟩
    intro w
    have ht := hTangent.2.1 (m μ-y) w.1 w.property
    refine ⟨ht.1,?_⟩
    exact ht.2.2.trans ((mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hResidual μ) (by positivity)).trans (by linarith))

                                      Literal module excerpt. Local names retain the surrounding theorem context, available with the complete folded theorem; these are proof ingredients, not extra public premises.

                                      7. Combine law and point movement

                                      Use the tangent-field joint estimate, substitute the actual mean sensitivity and residual budget, and dominate the chord by the angle. All costs are finite before applying toReal; the sum of the two coefficients plus one yields a single constant.

                                      \[\|G_\mu(w)-G_\nu(u)\|\le2M_1^2\sqrt Q+2(M_2+2M_1)R_0c(w,u)\le C_2(\sqrt Q+c(w,u)).\]
                                      Corresponding Lean step
                                        · intro μ ν hμ hν
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := hν
    refine ⟨(hMean μ ν).2.2.1,?_⟩
    intro w u
    have hm : ‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖ ≤ M₁*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := by
      simpa only [sub_sub_sub_cancel_right] using (hMean μ ν).2.2.2.1
    have hr := hResidual ν
    have ht := hTangent.2.2 (m μ-y) (m ν-y) w.1 u.1 w.property u.property
    have hpoint := (hAng.2.2.1 w u).2.2.2.1
    have ht' : ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
        A*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal+B₂*c (w,u) := by
      calc
        _ ≤ 2*M₁*‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖+
            2*(M₂+2*M₁)*‖m ν-y‖*‖w.1-u.1‖ := ht
        _ ≤ 2*M₁*(M₁*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal)+
            2*(M₂+2*M₁)*R₀*c (w,u) := by
          gcongr
        _ = _ := by dsimp [A,B₂]; ring
    apply ht'.trans
    have hs : 0 ≤ (Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
    have hc := hc0 (w,u)
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hA hc,mul_nonneg hB₂ hs]

    (∀ μ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ →

    ∀ μ ν : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν →

    apply (convex_closedBall (0 : E) 1).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le
      (fun z _ => (hF z).hasFDerivWithinAt) ?_

    change ‖F w.1‖ ≤ B
    dsimp [B]
    linarith
  have hAng := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost.unit_sphere_angular_cost_properties (E := E)

    (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧

  have hcB (z : S × S) : c z ≤ Real.pi := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).2.1

    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.QuadraticFeatureTangentGradient.quadratic_feature_potential_tangent_gradient
      F D hF M₁ M₂ hM₁ hM₂ hBound hLip

    ((hMean μ μ).2.2.2.2 y).1

                                      Source assumptions versus formal assumptions

                                      SourceActual LeanDifference kindWhy it matters
                                      Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure and H a complete real inner-product normed space. Let F:E→H have actual ambient Frechet derivative D(w):E→H for every w. Assume nonnegative M1,M2, an operator bound norm(D(w))<=M1 on the closed unit ball and an operator-Lipschitz bound norm(D(w)-D(u))<=M2 norm(w-u) there. Fix y in H. On the actual unit-norm subtype S define K(w)=F(w), angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)), the actual Bochner mean m(mu)=integral K dmu, V_mu(w)=2 inner(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G_mu(w)=2P_w D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) with the explicit projection P_w z=z−⟨z,w⟩w, which projects onto w-perpendicular when norm(w)=1. Let Q(mu,nu) be the literal extended nonnegative infimum of the quadratic angular cost over all actual couplings. There exist C1,C2>0, independent of probability laws and unit weights, such that for every actual parameter probability K is integrable, V_mu has the displayed ambient gradient 2D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) at every ambient w, and its projected G_mu is tangent and uniformly bounded by C1 at every unit weight. For every two actual parameter probabilities Q is finite and norm(G_mu(w)-G_nu(u))<=C2*(sqrt(Q).toReal+c(w,u)). Feature boundedness, strong measurability, feature Lipschitz control and residual budgets are derived inside the proof rather than assumed; the returned conclusions are feature integrability, actual ambient gradient, tangency/uniform bound, finite transport cost and the joint sensitivity estimate. The constants may depend on the displayed feature/derivative data, E,H and y. This is a generic feature-law theorem, not a concrete Gaussian scalar-data potential, installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length theorem.The exact adjacent signature retains the full displayed carrier and analytic data, actual Bochner law means, angular cost, extended all-coupling infimum and constant quantifier order.sameAmbient derivatives/operator bounds are explicit generic inputs only to the feature-law result; all feature-integrability/residual/cost estimates are derived. Angular geometry supplies properties of the actual cost. No intrinsic-path/manifold/Wasserstein API identification or chosen statistical instance is claimed.

                                      F and D plus their actual derivative/operator bounds remain explicit generic inputs. A specific model must produce them and identify its literal scalar potential with this Hilbert potential.; Angular all-coupling cost, tangent projection and actual ambient gradient are explicit. Identification with a chosen Riemannian-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length convention remains separate.; Auxiliary feature bounds, strong measurability and residual estimates are derived internally; they are not separately returned conjuncts. Constants may depend on E,H,F,D,M1,M2,y.

                                        Generic product-sphere calculus supplement, 2026-11-17 · public-support-source.json#support-12 (historical source) · licensed original

                                        Complete source statement and conditions

                                        Write \(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S_n=\{x\in E_n:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). The dimensions are natural numbers and may be zero. For every natural \(n,N\), every family \(V_i:M_{n,N}\to E_n\), and every configuration \(x\), sum the total sphere divergences of the sections \(y\mapsto V_i(x[i\leftarrow y])\) at \(x_i\). There is no factor \(1/N\); for \(N=0\) the sum is zero. No regularity or tangency is part of the definition. The ordinary product Riemannian divergence interpretation applies to jointly C¹ components satisfying pointwise tangency. The configuration \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) replaces coordinate \(i\) of \(x\) by \(y\) and leaves every other coordinate fixed. For \(G:S_n\to E_n\), define \(G^{\mathrm r}(z)=G(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\), with \(G^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\), and \(\operatorname{div}_S^{\mathrm{tot}}G(u)=\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)}\operatorname{deriv}_{\mathrm{tot}}[t\mapsto(G^{\mathrm r}(u+t e_j))_j](0)\). Here \(e_j\) is the standard Euclidean coordinate vector, and each total scalar derivative is the ordinary derivative where it exists and zero otherwise. Pointwise tangency means \(V_i(x)\perp x_i\) for every \(i,x\); joint C¹ refers to the ordinary finite product of the stereographic sphere smooth structures.

                                        • Use the indicated canonical real Euclidean, unit-sphere and finite-product carriers; no positive-dimension restriction is imposed.
                                        • This is a definition or abbreviation. It imposes no unstated regularity, tangency, integrability or probability hypothesis.

                                        Complete source statement and conditions

                                        Write \(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S_n=\{x\in E_n:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). The dimensions are natural numbers and may be zero. For every natural \(n,N\), every real function \(f:M_{n,N}\to\mathbb R\), every coordinate \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}N\), and every configuration \(x\), fix the other coordinates and apply the total sphere-gradient definition to the section \(y\mapsto f(x[i\leftarrow y])\) at \(x_i\). No regularity is part of the definition. Under joint intrinsic C¹ regularity it is the ordinary coordinate intrinsic gradient. For \(N=0\) there is no coordinate argument. The configuration \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) replaces coordinate \(i\) of \(x\) by \(y\) and leaves every other coordinate fixed. For \(g:S_n\to\mathbb R\), define \(g^{\mathrm r}(z)=g(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\), with \(g^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\), and \(\nabla_S^{\mathrm{tot}}g(u)=P_u\mathcal R^{-1}(D_{\mathrm{tot}}g^{\mathrm r}(u))\). Here \(P_uv=v-\langle u,v\rangle u\), \(\mathcal R^{-1}\) is the inverse real Euclidean Riesz isometry, and \(D_{\mathrm{tot}}\) is the ordinary Fréchet derivative where it exists and zero otherwise. Joint intrinsic C¹ refers to the ordinary finite product of the stereographic sphere smooth structures.

                                        • Use the indicated canonical real Euclidean, unit-sphere and finite-product carriers; no positive-dimension restriction is imposed.
                                        • This is a definition or abbreviation. It imposes no unstated regularity, tangency, integrability or probability hypothesis.

                                          Library supplement: Integration by parts on a finite product of unit spheres

                                          Generic exposition of classical sphere calculus; no primary-textbook completion or novelty claim.

                                          Generic product-sphere calculus supplement, 2026-11-17 · Main integration-by-parts identity (historical source) · licensed original

                                          Complete source statement and conditions

                                          For arbitrary \(n,N\in\mathbb N\), let \(E=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S=\{x\in E:\|x\|=1\}\) and \(M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). Equip \(S\) with its induced Euclidean metric and stereographic smooth structure, and equip \(M\) with their product structures and the normalized polar product measure \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\) defined below. For every intrinsically C¹ real function \(f\) on \(M\) and every family of intrinsically C¹ maps \(V_i:M\to E\) satisfying \(\langle x_i,V_i(x)\rangle=0\) at every configuration and coordinate, all three displayed integrands are integrable and the following identities hold. The operators are the actual tangent gradient and tangent divergence, specified through canonical radial extension; their regularity and intrinsic interpretation are proved internally.

                                          • \(n,N\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary, with no positivity restriction. Thus the ambient dimension is \(n+1\); \(n=0\) gives the two-point sphere and \(N=0\) gives a one-point empty product.
                                          • The scalar field is \(\mathbb R\). All norms, inner products, tangent projections and manifold metrics are induced by the Euclidean structure. Regularity means regularity in the usual stereographic sphere charts and their finite product charts.
                                          • The reference measure is exactly \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\), with \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau\) and \(\tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere}\). Its finite nonzero mass and probability normalization are proved internally; they are not extra inputs.
                                          • For every supplied \(f:M\to\mathbb R\), assume \(f\in C^1(M)\). For every supplied family \(V_i:M\to E\), assume each \(V_i\in C^1(M;E)\), jointly in the complete configuration.
                                          • Tangency holds at every configuration and every coordinate: \(\langle x_i,V_i(x)\rangle=0\) for all \(x\in M\) and \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}N\). This is a pointwise hypothesis, not an almost-everywhere substitute.

                                          Integration by parts on a finite product of unit spheres

                                          \[\begin{gathered}\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad f\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle\in L^1(\mu),\\\int_M\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=0,\\\int_Mf\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=-\int_M\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]

                                          Samplinglib mathematical lesson

                                          Integration by parts on a finite product of unit spheres

                                          Read this first

                                          Mathematical statement

                                          For arbitrary \(n,N\in\mathbb N\), let \(E=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S=\{x\in E:\|x\|=1\}\) and \(M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). Equip \(S\) with its induced Euclidean metric and stereographic smooth structure, and equip \(M\) with their product structures and the normalized polar product measure \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\) defined below. For every intrinsically C¹ real function \(f\) on \(M\) and every family of intrinsically C¹ maps \(V_i:M\to E\) satisfying \(\langle x_i,V_i(x)\rangle=0\) at every configuration and coordinate, all three displayed integrands are integrable and the following identities hold. The operators are the actual tangent gradient and tangent divergence, specified through canonical radial extension; their regularity and intrinsic interpretation are proved internally.

                                          \[\begin{gathered}\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad f\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle\in L^1(\mu),\\\int_M\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=0,\\\int_Mf\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=-\int_M\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]
                                          Lean statement · sphere_product_tangential_integration_by_parts

                                          The exact type has only n, N, f, V, their intrinsic C¹ regularity, and pointwise tangency. The three integrability statements and both integral identities are conclusions.

Named hypotheses are mathematical premises, not facts established by this declaration.                                           Download module (.lean)
                                          theorem sphere_product_tangential_integration_by_parts
    {n N : ℕ}
    (f : SphereConfiguration n N → ℝ)
    (V : Fin N → SphereConfiguration n N → SphereAmbient n)
    (hf : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 f)
    (hV : ∀ i, ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 (V i))
    (hTangent : ∀ (x : SphereConfiguration n N) (i : Fin N),
      inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (V i x) = 0) :
    Integrable (sphereProductDivergence V) (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereProductDivergence V x)
      (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => ∑ i : Fin N, inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x))
      (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
    (∫ x, sphereProductDivergence V x ∂(sphereProductMeasure n N)) = 0 ∧
    (∫ x, f x * sphereProductDivergence V x ∂(sphereProductMeasure n N)) =
      -(∫ x, ∑ i : Fin N, inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x)
        ∂(sphereProductMeasure n N))

                                          Exact module and namespace context

                                          This supplies the integral identities for C¹ tangent fields on a finite product of spheres with its actual normalized product measure. Proof strategy: Fix the normalized surface measure; Obtain radial regularity from the sphere charts; Identify the actual tangent differential and gradient; Identify divergence with the induced tangent trace; Build an annular field and compute its divergence; Use ambient divergence and polar transport; Apply the product rule on one sphere; Transport each coordinate identity to the finite product; Sum the coordinates and conclude integration by parts.

                                          Full assumptions and notation

                                          All objects and hypotheses

                                          • \(n,N\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary, with no positivity restriction. Thus the ambient dimension is \(n+1\); \(n=0\) gives the two-point sphere and \(N=0\) gives a one-point empty product.
                                          • The scalar field is \(\mathbb R\). All norms, inner products, tangent projections and manifold metrics are induced by the Euclidean structure. Regularity means regularity in the usual stereographic sphere charts and their finite product charts.
                                          • The reference measure is exactly \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\), with \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau\) and \(\tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere}\). Its finite nonzero mass and probability normalization are proved internally; they are not extra inputs.
                                          • For every supplied \(f:M\to\mathbb R\), assume \(f\in C^1(M)\). For every supplied family \(V_i:M\to E\), assume each \(V_i\in C^1(M;E)\), jointly in the complete configuration.
                                          • Tangency holds at every configuration and every coordinate: \(\langle x_i,V_i(x)\rangle=0\) for all \(x\in M\) and \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}N\). This is a pointwise hypothesis, not an almost-everywhere substitute.

                                          Notation and interpretation

                                          \(E,S,M,\mu\)

                                          The ambient space is real Euclidean space; the sphere carries its induced metric and usual stereographic smooth structure. The configuration has one sphere coordinate for each element of \(\operatorname{Fin}N\). The measure is fixed by Euclidean volume, not supplied arbitrarily.

                                          \[E=\mathbb R^{n+1},\quad S=\{z\in E:\|z\|=1\},\quad M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N},\quad \tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere},\quad \sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau,\quad\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}.\]
                                          \(h^{\mathrm r}\)

                                          This is the specified canonical radial extension of a sphere function with values in a real normed space. Its zero value at the origin totalizes the function. Derivatives defining sphere operators are taken at unit vectors, inside the open nonzero region.

                                          \[h^{\mathrm r}(z)=\begin{cases}h(z/\|z\|),&z\ne0,\\0,&z=0.\end{cases}\]
                                          \(P_x,\nabla_S,\operatorname{div}_S\)

                                          The projection is onto the actual tangent hyperplane. The gradient uses the Euclidean Riesz representative of the radial differential. For a tangent C¹ field, the displayed divergence equals the intrinsic divergence: its radial differential agrees with the sphere differential, kills the normal, and has the same trace as the induced tangent endomorphism. This interpretation of divergence requires tangency.

                                          \[P_xv=v-\langle x,v\rangle x,\qquad \nabla_Sh(x)=P_x\nabla_Eh^{\mathrm r}(x),\qquad\operatorname{div}_SW(x)=\operatorname{tr}_E D(W^{\mathrm r})(x).\]
                                          \(\nabla_i f,\operatorname{div}_M V\)

                                          Write \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) for replacement of coordinate \(i\) by \(y\). Differentiate that sphere coordinate while holding every other coordinate fixed. The pairing and divergence are sums, with no factor \(1/N\).

                                          \[\nabla_i f(x)=\nabla_S[y\mapsto f(x[i\leftarrow y])](x_i),\qquad\operatorname{div}_M V(x)=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\operatorname{div}_S[y\mapsto V_i(x[i\leftarrow y])](x_i).\]
                                          • Each integral uses \(\mu\); all sums run over \(\operatorname{Fin}N\). There is no empirical averaging factor.
                                          • The measure inverse is taken in the nonnegative extended reals. Its finite positive denominator is established before normalization is used.

                                          Mathematical proof

                                          Open a step to read its argument and formula.

                                          1. Fix the normalized surface measure

                                          Euclidean dimension \(n+1\) is positive even when \(n=0\), so the polar measure has finite, nonzero total mass. Scale it by the reciprocal mass, then take the actual finite product. This normalization is an explicit measure construction, not an unproved integration-by-parts premise.

                                          \[0<\tau(S)<\infty,\qquad\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau,\qquad\sigma(S)=1,\qquad\mu(M)=1.\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          instance sphereSurfaceMeasure_isFinite (n : ℕ) :
    IsFiniteMeasure (sphereSurfaceMeasure n) := by
  unfold sphereSurfaceMeasure
  infer_instance

private theorem sphereSurfaceMeasure_mass_ne_zero (n : ℕ) :
    sphereSurfaceMeasure n univ ≠ 0 := by
  apply Measure.measure_univ_ne_zero.mpr
  exact Measure.toSphere_ne_zero (volume : Measure (SphereAmbient n))

instance sphereUniformMeasure_isProbability (n : ℕ) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (sphereUniformMeasure n) where
  measure_univ := by
    rw [sphereUniformMeasure, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    exact ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel (sphereSurfaceMeasure_mass_ne_zero n) (measure_ne_top _ _)

instance sphereProductMeasure_isProbability (n N : ℕ) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (sphereProductMeasure n N) := by
  unfold sphereProductMeasure
  infer_instance

                                          2. Obtain radial regularity from the sphere charts

                                          The normalization map \(R(z)=z/\|z\|\) is smooth on \(E\setminus\{0\}\). Viewed as a sphere-valued map, it is smooth in the actual stereographic charts. Composing \(R\) with an intrinsic C¹ function or field gives its C¹ canonical radial extension near each unit vector. The same coordinatewise construction on the open set where every coordinate is nonzero handles joint product regularity.

                                          \[R:E\setminus\{0\}\longrightarrow S,\quad h^{\mathrm r}=h\circ R,\quad h\in C^1(S;A)\Longrightarrow h^{\mathrm r}\in C^1(E\setminus\{0\};A),\quad h^{\mathrm r}|_S=h.\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          private theorem contDiffAt_radialExtension {n : ℕ} {A : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A] {k : ℕ∞ω}
    (f : SpherePoint n → A) (hf : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, A) k f)
    {x : SphereAmbient n} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ k (sphereRadialExtension f) x := by
  let x' : nonzeroDomain n := ⟨x, hx⟩
  have h := hf.comp (contMDiff_radialProjection (n := n) k)
  have heq : (fun z : nonzeroDomain n => sphereRadialExtension f (z : SphereAmbient n)) =
      (fun z : nonzeroDomain n => f (homeomorphUnitSphereProd (SphereAmbient n) z).1) := by
    funext z
    have hz : (z : SphereAmbient n) ≠ 0 := z.property
    simp only [sphereRadialExtension, dif_neg hz]
    rfl
  have hlocal : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 𝓘(ℝ, A) k
      (fun z : nonzeroDomain n => sphereRadialExtension f (z : SphereAmbient n)) x' := by
    rw [heq]
    exact h x'
  exact (contMDiffAt_subtype_iff.mp hlocal).contDiffAt

                                          This is one literal contiguous excerpt from the frozen module. The complete declaration and supporting implementations remain in the folded Lean proof.

                                          3. Identify the actual tangent differential and gradient

                                          Let \(J_x\) be the differential of the sphere inclusion and \(D_x=D(h^{\mathrm r})(x)\). Differentiating radial constancy gives \(D_xx=0\). The manifold chain rule and restriction identity give \(D_xJ_x=dh_x\), and orthogonal decomposition gives \(D_xP_x=D_x\). The projected Riesz gradient therefore pairs with the actual sphere differential on every tangent vector.

                                          \[D_xx=0,\qquad D_xJ_x=dh_x,\qquad D_xP_x=D_x,\qquad\langle\nabla_Sh(x),J_xu\rangle=dh_x[u].\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          private theorem radialExtension_actual_differential {n : ℕ} {A : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A]
    (f : SpherePoint n → A) (hf : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, A) 1 f)
    (x : SpherePoint n) :
    let D := fderiv ℝ (sphereRadialExtension f) (x : SphereAmbient n)
    let J := mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) x
    let P := (ℝ ∙ (x : SphereAmbient n))ᗮ.starProjection
    D (x : SphereAmbient n) = 0 ∧ D.comp J = mvfderiv (𝓡 n) f x ∧ D.comp P = D := by
  let : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ (SphereAmbient n) = n + 1) := ⟨by simp [SphereAmbient]⟩
  dsimp only
  let D := fderiv ℝ (sphereRadialExtension f) (x : SphereAmbient n)
  have hd := (contDiffAt_radialExtension f hf (ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere x)).differentiableAt one_ne_zero
  have hnormal : D (x : SphereAmbient n) = 0 := by
    let l : ℝ → SphereAmbient n := fun t => (1 + t) • (x : SphereAmbient n)
    have hl : HasDerivAt l (x : SphereAmbient n) 0 := by
      simpa [l] using (((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).const_add 1).smul_const (x : SphereAmbient n))
    have hd' : DifferentiableAt ℝ (sphereRadialExtension f) (l 0) := by simpa [l] using hd
    have hpos : ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in 𝓝 0, 0 < 1 + t :=
      (isOpen_lt continuous_const (continuous_const.add continuous_id)).mem_nhds (by simp)
    have he : sphereRadialExtension f ∘ l =ᶠ[𝓝 0] fun _ => sphereRadialExtension f (x : SphereAmbient n) :=
      hpos.mono fun t ht => radialExtension_pos_smul f (x : SphereAmbient n) ht
    have hdv := hd'.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt 0 hl
    have hz := (hasDerivAt_const 0 (sphereRadialExtension f (x : SphereAmbient n))).congr_of_eventuallyEq he
    simpa [l, D] using hdv.unique hz
  have he : sphereRadialExtension f ∘ ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) = f :=
    funext (radialExtension_on_sphere f)
  have hco := (contMDiff_coe_sphere (n := n) (m := 1) x).mdifferentiableAt one_ne_zero
  have hchain : D.comp (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) x) =
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) f x := by
    have hc := mfderiv_comp x hd.mdifferentiableAt hco
    rw [he, mfderiv_eq_fderiv] at hc
    exact hc.symm
  refine ⟨hnormal, hchain, ?_⟩
  ext v
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val,
    Submodule.starProjection_unit_singleton ℝ (norm_eq_of_mem_sphere x), map_sub, map_smul,
    hnormal, smul_zero, sub_zero]

/-- The projected gradient pairs with the actual sphere differential, not only
with an arbitrarily named operator. -/
private theorem tangentGradient_pairing_mvfderiv {n : ℕ}
    (f : SpherePoint n → ℝ) (hf : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 f)
    (x : SpherePoint n) (u : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x) :
    inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x)
      (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) x u) =
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) f x u := by
  let : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ (SphereAmbient n) = n + 1) := ⟨by simp [SphereAmbient]⟩
  let J := mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) x
  have hmem : J u ∈ (ℝ ∙ (x : SphereAmbient n))ᗮ := by
    rw [← range_mvfderiv_subtypeVal (n := n) x]
    exact ⟨u, rfl⟩
  rw [tangentGradient_pairing f x (J u)
    (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right.mp hmem)]
  exact congrArg (fun T : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x →L[ℝ] ℝ => T u)
    (radialExtension_actual_differential f hf x).2.1

                                          This is one literal contiguous excerpt from the frozen module. The complete declaration and supporting implementations remain in the folded Lean proof.

                                          4. Identify divergence with the induced tangent trace

                                          Let \(K_x=x^\perp\), let \(\iota_x:K_x\hookrightarrow E\) be inclusion, and let \(Q_x:E\to K_x\) be the orthogonal projection with codomain restricted to the tangent subspace. The projected derivative \(Q_xD_x\iota_x\) is an actual endomorphism of \(K_x\). The preceding differential identity identifies it with the induced covariant derivative when the field is tangent. Cyclic invariance of trace and \(D_xP_x=D_x\) prove equality with the ambient trace. For a non-tangent map, this is not the divergence of its tangent projection.

                                          \[\operatorname{div}_SW(x)=\operatorname{tr}_E D_x=\operatorname{tr}_{K_x}(Q_xD_x\iota_x),\qquad D_x=D(W^{\mathrm r})(x).\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          private theorem tangentDivergence_eq_tangent_trace {n : ℕ}
    (V : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n)
    (hV : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V) (x : SpherePoint n) :
    let K := (ℝ ∙ (x : SphereAmbient n))ᗮ
    let D := fderiv ℝ (sphereRadialExtension V) (x : SphereAmbient n)
    sphereTangentDivergence V x =
      LinearMap.trace ℝ K (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto.toLinearMap.comp
        (D.toLinearMap.comp K.subtype)) := by
  intro K D
  have htrace : sphereTangentDivergence V x = LinearMap.trace ℝ (SphereAmbient n) D.toLinearMap := by
    rw [tangentDivergence_eq_fderiv_trace V hV x,
      LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace ℝ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ).toBasis]
    simp [Matrix.trace, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis,
      OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, D]
  have hfactor : D.toLinearMap.comp (K.subtype.comp K.orthogonalProjectionOnto.toLinearMap) =
      D.toLinearMap := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro v
    change D (K.starProjection v) = D v
    exact congrArg (fun T : SphereAmbient n →L[ℝ] SphereAmbient n => T v)
      (radialExtension_actual_differential V hV x).2.2
  calc
    sphereTangentDivergence V x = LinearMap.trace ℝ (SphereAmbient n) D.toLinearMap := htrace
    _ = LinearMap.trace ℝ (SphereAmbient n)
        (D.toLinearMap.comp (K.subtype.comp K.orthogonalProjectionOnto.toLinearMap)) :=
      congrArg (LinearMap.trace ℝ (SphereAmbient n)) hfactor.symm
    _ = LinearMap.trace ℝ K (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto.toLinearMap.comp
        (D.toLinearMap.comp K.subtype)) :=
      LinearMap.trace_comp_comm' K.orthogonalProjectionOnto.toLinearMap (D.toLinearMap.comp K.subtype)

                                          5. Build an annular field and compute its divergence

                                          Choose the fixed smooth nonnegative cutoff \(\chi(r)=\mathrm{smoothUnitCutoff}(r^2-4)\), and form \(F(z)=\chi(\|z\|)W^{\mathrm r}(z)\). It vanishes near zero and outside a bounded annulus, so the derived local regularity gives a globally C¹, compactly supported field. Tangency removes the radial cutoff derivative; radial homogeneity scales the remaining derivative by \(1/r\).

                                          \[F(r\zeta)=\chi(r)W(\zeta),\qquad\operatorname{div}_E F(r\zeta)=\frac{\chi(r)}r\operatorname{div}_SW(\zeta)\quad(r>0,\ \zeta\in S).\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          private theorem divergence_annularExtension_polar {n : ℕ}
    (V : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n)
    (hV : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V)
    (hTangent : ∀ x : SpherePoint n, inner ℝ (x : SphereAmbient n) (V x) = 0)
    (x : SpherePoint n) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.Divergence.coordinateDivergence
      (annularExtension V) (r • (x : SphereAmbient n)) =
      (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.Cutoff.smoothUnitCutoff (r ^ 2 - 4) / r) *
        sphereTangentDivergence V x := by
  rw [divergence_annularExtension V hV hTangent _ (smul_ne_zero hr.ne' (ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere x)),
    divergence_radialExtension_pos_smul V hV x hr]
  simp [annularCutoff, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hr, norm_eq_of_mem_sphere,
    div_eq_mul_inv, mul_assoc]

                                          6. Use ambient divergence and polar transport

                                          The existing compact-support divergence theorem gives zero ambient integral. The existing polar change of variables and Fubini separate a radial factor from the surface divergence integral. The factor is strictly positive: its continuous nonnegative integrand is positive at radius two. It is finite because the cutoff is supported away from zero in a bounded annulus. Cancel the factor, then scale the surface integral to the normalized measure.

                                          \[0=\int_E\operatorname{div}_EF\,dz=c_n\int_S\operatorname{div}_SW\,d\tau,\qquad c_n=\int_0^\infty r^n\frac{\chi(r)}r\,dr>0,\qquad\int_S\operatorname{div}_SW\,d\sigma=0.\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          private theorem integral_tangentDivergence_surface_eq_zero {n : ℕ}
    (V : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n)
    (hV : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V)
    (hTangent : ∀ x : SpherePoint n, inner ℝ (x : SphereAmbient n) (V x) = 0) :
    (∫ x, sphereTangentDivergence V x ∂sphereSurfaceMeasure n) = 0 := by
  let F := annularExtension V
  let dF := Divergence.coordinateDivergence F
  have hF : ContDiff ℝ 1 F := contDiff_annularExtension V hV
  have hFc : HasCompactSupport F := hasCompactSupport_annularExtension V
  have htrace : dF = fun x => ∑ j : Fin (n + 1),
      fderiv ℝ F x (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) j := by
    funext x
    exact Divergence.coordinateDivergence_eq_sum_fderiv_apply_of_differentiableAt
      (hF.differentiable one_ne_zero x)
  have hDc : Continuous dF := by
    rw [htrace]
    apply continuous_finsetSum
    intro j _
    exact (PiLp.proj (p := 2) (𝕜 := ℝ) (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => ℝ) j).continuous.comp
      ((hF.continuous_fderiv one_ne_zero).clm_apply continuous_const)
  have hDs : HasCompactSupport dF := by
    rw [htrace]
    exact (hFc.fderiv ℝ).comp_left (g := fun L : SphereAmbient n →L[ℝ] SphereAmbient n =>
      ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), L (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) j) (by simp)
  have hI : Integrable dF := hDc.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hDs
  let e := PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => ℝ)
  let G : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ := fun x => e (F (e.symm x))
  have hzeroRaw := Divergence.integral_coordinateDivergence_wrapped_eq_zero_of_contDiff_of_hasCompactSupport
    G (e.contDiff.comp (hF.comp e.symm.contDiff))
      ((hFc.comp_homeomorph e.symm.toHomeomorph).comp_left e.map_zero)
  have hzero : (∫ x, dF x) = 0 := by
    have htransport := (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp (Fin (n + 1))).integral_comp
      (MeasurableEquiv.measurableEmbedding (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ))) dF
    simpa [dF, G, e] using htransport.symm.trans hzeroRaw
  let τ := sphereSurfaceMeasure n
  let q : SpherePoint n × Ioi (0 : ℝ) → ℝ := fun z => dF (z.2.1 • (z.1 : SphereAmbient n))
  have hsub : Integrable (fun x : ({0}ᶜ : Set (SphereAmbient n)) => dF x.1)
      ((volume : Measure (SphereAmbient n)).comap Subtype.val) :=
    (integrableOn_iff_comap_subtypeVal (measurableSet_singleton 0).compl).mp hI.restrict
  have hmp := (volume : Measure (SphereAmbient n)).measurePreserving_homeomorphUnitSphereProd
  have hcomp : q ∘ homeomorphUnitSphereProd (SphereAmbient n) =
      fun x : ({0}ᶜ : Set (SphereAmbient n)) => dF x.1 := by
    funext x
    change dF ((homeomorphUnitSphereProd (SphereAmbient n)).symm
      (homeomorphUnitSphereProd (SphereAmbient n) x)).1 = dF x.1
    rw [Homeomorph.symm_apply_apply]
  have hq : Integrable q (τ.prod (Measure.volumeIoiPow n)) := by
    have h := (hmp.integrable_comp_emb (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding _)).mp (hcomp.symm ▸ hsub)
    simpa [SphereAmbient, τ, sphereSurfaceMeasure] using h
  have hqzero : (∫ z, q z ∂τ.prod (Measure.volumeIoiPow n)) = 0 := by
    have htransport := hmp.integral_comp (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding _) q
    change (∫ x : ({0}ᶜ : Set (SphereAmbient n)),
      (q ∘ homeomorphUnitSphereProd (SphereAmbient n)) x
        ∂(volume : Measure (SphereAmbient n)).comap Subtype.val) = _ at htransport
    rw [hcomp, integral_subtype_comap (measurableSet_singleton _).compl,
      restrict_compl_singleton] at htransport
    have ht : (∫ x, dF x) = ∫ z, q z ∂τ.prod (Measure.volumeIoiPow n) := by
      simpa [SphereAmbient, τ, sphereSurfaceMeasure] using htransport
    exact ht.symm.trans hzero
  have hqval (x : SpherePoint n) (r : Ioi (0 : ℝ)) : q (x, r) =
      (Cutoff.smoothUnitCutoff (r.1 ^ 2 - 4) / r.1) * sphereTangentDivergence V x :=
    divergence_annularExtension_polar V hV hTangent x r.2
  have hfactor : (∫ z, q z ∂τ.prod (Measure.volumeIoiPow n)) =
      (∫ r in Ioi (0 : ℝ), radialIntegrationWeight n r) *
        ∫ x, sphereTangentDivergence V x ∂τ := by
    rw [integral_prod_symm q hq]
    simp_rw [hqval, integral_const_mul]
    rw [integral_mul_const, radialIntegrationWeight_polar_mass]
  have hmulzero := hfactor.symm.trans hqzero
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hmulzero).resolve_left (ne_of_gt (radialIntegrationWeight_integral_pos n))

                                          7. Apply the product rule on one sphere

                                          Radial extension commutes with scalar multiplication. The ordinary derivative product rule and the tangent-gradient pairing give the displayed divergence identity. Apply the zero-divergence result to the tangent field \(hW\). Continuity on the compact sphere supplies each integrability statement. This proves the source single-sphere intermediate identity; the finite-product proof below uses the equivalent zero-divergence-plus-product-rule route.

                                          \[\operatorname{div}_S(hW)=h\operatorname{div}_SW+\langle\nabla_Sh,W\rangle,\qquad\int_Sh\operatorname{div}_SW\,d\sigma=-\int_S\langle\nabla_Sh,W\rangle\,d\sigma.\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          private theorem singleSphere_integration_by_parts {n : ℕ}
    (f : SpherePoint n → ℝ) (V : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n)
    (hf : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 f)
    (hV : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V)
    (hTangent : ∀ x : SpherePoint n, inner ℝ (x : SphereAmbient n) (V x) = 0) :
    Integrable (sphereTangentDivergence V) (sphereUniformMeasure n) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x) (sphereUniformMeasure n) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) (sphereUniformMeasure n) ∧
    (∫ x, sphereTangentDivergence V x ∂sphereUniformMeasure n) = 0 ∧
    (∫ x, f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x ∂sphereUniformMeasure n) =
      -(∫ x, inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x) ∂sphereUniformMeasure n) := by
  have hW : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 (fun x => f x • V x) := hf.smul hV
  have hWTangent (x : SpherePoint n) : inner ℝ (x : SphereAmbient n) (f x • V x) = 0 := by
    rw [inner_smul_right, hTangent x, mul_zero]
  have hmul : Continuous (fun x => f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x) :=
    hf.continuous.mul (continuous_tangentDivergence V hV)
  have hpair : Continuous (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) := by
    have heq : (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) =
        fun x => sphereTangentDivergence (fun y => f y • V y) x - f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x := by
      funext x
      rw [tangentDivergence_smul f V hf hV hTangent x]
      ring
    rw [heq]
    exact (continuous_tangentDivergence _ hW).sub hmul
  have hImul : Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x) (sphereUniformMeasure n) := by
    simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using hmul.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
      (μ := sphereUniformMeasure n) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
  have hIpair : Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) (sphereUniformMeasure n) := by
    simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using hpair.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
      (μ := sphereUniformMeasure n) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
  refine ⟨integrable_tangentDivergence V hV, hImul, hIpair,
    integral_tangentDivergence_eq_zero V hV hTangent, ?_⟩
  have hzero := integral_tangentDivergence_eq_zero (fun x => f x • V x) hW hWTangent
  simp_rw [tangentDivergence_smul f V hf hV hTangent] at hzero
  rw [integral_add hImul hIpair] at hzero
  linarith

                                          8. Transport each coordinate identity to the finite product

                                          Joint C¹ regularity gives continuous section derivatives through the joint radial extension. For any coordinate \(i\), split the product into that sphere and the remaining configuration \(z\) by the actual measure-preserving coordinate reordering. Write \(x(z,y)\) for the configuration with coordinate \(i\) equal to \(y\) and all others supplied by \(z\), and set \(W_{i,z}(y)=V_i(x(z,y))\). Fubini applies to the continuous divergence integrand on the compact product. Its inner sphere integral is zero. There is no coordinate to consider when \(N=0\).

                                          \[\int_M\operatorname{div}_iV_i\,d\mu=\int_{M_{\widehat i}}\left[\int_S\operatorname{div}_S W_{i,z}(y)\,d\sigma(y)\right]d\mu_{\widehat i}(z)=0,\qquad\mu_{\widehat i}=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}\sigma.\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          private theorem integral_configuration_divergence_coordinate_eq_zero {n N : ℕ}
    (V : SphereConfiguration n N → SphereAmbient n)
    (hV : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V)
    (i : Fin N)
    (hTangent : ∀ x : SphereConfiguration n N, inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (V x) = 0) :
    (∫ x, sphereTangentDivergence (fun z => V (Function.update x i z)) (x i)
      ∂sphereProductMeasure n N) = 0 := by
  cases N with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 i
  | succ N =>
    let σ := sphereUniformMeasure n
    let μ := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin N => σ)
    let H : SphereConfiguration n (N + 1) → ℝ := fun x =>
      sphereTangentDivergence (fun z => V (Function.update x i z)) (x i)
    have hI : Integrable H (sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) := by
      simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using
        (continuous_configuration_divergence_coordinate V hV i).continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
          (μ := sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
    let e := MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ : Fin (N + 1) => SpherePoint n) i
    have hmp : MeasurePreserving e (sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) (σ.prod μ) :=
      measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => σ) i
    let q := H ∘ e.symm
    have hq : Integrable q (σ.prod μ) :=
      (hmp.symm.integrable_comp_emb e.symm.measurableEmbedding).mpr hI
    have hqval (y : SpherePoint n) (z : Fin N → SpherePoint n) : q (y, z) =
        sphereTangentDivergence (fun w => V (i.insertNth w z)) y := by
      change sphereTangentDivergence
        (fun w => V (Function.update (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z) i w)) ((i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z) i) = _
      simp only [Fin.insertNth_apply_same, Fin.update_insertNth]
    have hinner (z : Fin N → SpherePoint n) : (∫ y, q (y, z) ∂σ) = 0 := by
      let x0 : SpherePoint n := ⟨EuclideanSpace.single 0 (1 : ℝ), by simp⟩
      have hs : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) (sphereProductModel n (N + 1)) 1
          (fun y => i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z) := by
        have h := contMDiff_sphereSection 1 (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) x0 z) i
        simpa only [Fin.update_insertNth] using h
      have hW : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1
          (fun y => V (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z)) := hV.comp hs
      have hWT (y : SpherePoint n) : inner ℝ (y : SphereAmbient n) (V (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z)) = 0 := by
        simpa only [Fin.insertNth_apply_same] using hTangent (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z)
      simp_rw [hqval]
      exact integral_tangentDivergence_eq_zero _ hW hWT
    calc
      (∫ x, H x ∂sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) = ∫ z, q z ∂σ.prod μ :=
        (hmp.symm.integral_comp e.symm.measurableEmbedding H).symm
      _ = ∫ z, ∫ y, q (y, z) ∂σ ∂μ := integral_prod_symm q hq
      _ = 0 := by simp only [hinner, integral_zero]

                                          9. Sum the coordinates and conclude integration by parts

                                          Sum the coordinate zero integrals. The product rule gives the divergence of the pointwise field \(fV\). Both divergences and \(f\operatorname{div}_M V\) are continuous on the compact configuration space, so their difference—the gradient pairing—is also continuous and integrable. Integrating the product rule yields the two claimed identities and the three explicit integrability conclusions.

                                          \[\operatorname{div}_M(fV)=f\operatorname{div}_MV+\sum_i\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle,\qquad\int_M\operatorname{div}_MV\,d\mu=0,\qquad\int_Mf\operatorname{div}_MV\,d\mu=-\int_M\sum_i\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle\,d\mu.\]
                                          Corresponding Lean step
                                          theorem sphere_product_tangential_integration_by_parts
    {n N : ℕ}
    (f : SphereConfiguration n N → ℝ)
    (V : Fin N → SphereConfiguration n N → SphereAmbient n)
    (hf : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 f)
    (hV : ∀ i, ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 (V i))
    (hTangent : ∀ (x : SphereConfiguration n N) (i : Fin N),
      inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (V i x) = 0) :
    Integrable (sphereProductDivergence V) (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereProductDivergence V x)
      (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => ∑ i : Fin N, inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x))
      (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
    (∫ x, sphereProductDivergence V x ∂(sphereProductMeasure n N)) = 0 ∧
    (∫ x, f x * sphereProductDivergence V x ∂(sphereProductMeasure n N)) =
      -(∫ x, ∑ i : Fin N, inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x)
        ∂(sphereProductMeasure n N)) := by
  have hW (i : Fin N) : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1
      (fun x => f x • V i x) := hf.smul (hV i)
  have hWT (x : SphereConfiguration n N) (i : Fin N) :
      inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (f x • V i x) = 0 := by
    rw [inner_smul_right, hTangent x i, mul_zero]
  have hmul : Continuous (fun x => f x * sphereProductDivergence V x) :=
    hf.continuous.mul (continuous_sphereProductDivergence V hV)
  have hpair : Continuous (fun x => ∑ i : Fin N,
      inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x)) := by
    have heq : (fun x => ∑ i : Fin N, inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x)) =
        fun x => sphereProductDivergence (fun i y => f y • V i y) x - f x * sphereProductDivergence V x := by
      funext x
      rw [sphereProductDivergence_smul f V hf hV hTangent x]
      ring
    rw [heq]
    exact (continuous_sphereProductDivergence _ hW).sub hmul
  have hI : Integrable (sphereProductDivergence V) (sphereProductMeasure n N) := by
    simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using
      (continuous_sphereProductDivergence V hV).continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
        (μ := sphereProductMeasure n N) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
  have hImul : Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereProductDivergence V x) (sphereProductMeasure n N) := by
    simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using hmul.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
      (μ := sphereProductMeasure n N) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
  have hIpair : Integrable (fun x => ∑ i : Fin N,
      inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x)) (sphereProductMeasure n N) := by
    simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using hpair.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
      (μ := sphereProductMeasure n N) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
  refine ⟨hI, hImul, hIpair, integral_sphereProductDivergence_eq_zero V hV hTangent, ?_⟩
  have hzero := integral_sphereProductDivergence_eq_zero (fun i x => f x • V i x) hW hWT
  simp_rw [sphereProductDivergence_smul f V hf hV hTangent] at hzero
  rw [integral_add hImul hIpair] at hzero
  linarith

                                          private theorem contMDiff_radialProjection {n : ℕ} (k : ℕ∞ω) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) (𝓡 n) k
      (fun x : nonzeroDomain n => (homeomorphUnitSphereProd (SphereAmbient n) x).1) := by
  let : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ (SphereAmbient n) = n + 1) := ⟨by simp [SphereAmbient]⟩
  let U := nonzeroDomain n
  let r : U → SphereAmbient n := fun x => ‖(x : SphereAmbient n)‖⁻¹ • (x : SphereAmbient n)
  have hx (x : U) : (x : SphereAmbient n) ≠ 0 := by
    exact x.property
  have hr : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) k r := by
    intro x
    have hn : ContDiffAt ℝ k (fun y : SphereAmbient n => ‖y‖⁻¹ • y) (x : SphereAmbient n) :=
      ((contDiffAt_norm ℝ (hx x)).inv (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (hx x))).smul contDiffAt_id
    exact hn.contMDiffAt.comp x (contMDiff_subtype_val x)
  have hmem (x : U) : r x ∈ sphere (0 : SphereAmbient n) 1 := by
    rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm]
    simp [r, norm_smul, norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (hx x)]
  have hr' : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) (𝓡 n) k
      (Set.codRestrict r (sphere (0 : SphereAmbient n) 1) hmem) :=
    hr.codRestrict_sphere (n := n) hmem
  have heq : (fun x : U => (homeomorphUnitSphereProd (SphereAmbient n) x).1) =
      Set.codRestrict r (sphere (0 : SphereAmbient n) 1) hmem := by
    funext x
    apply Subtype.ext
    change (1 : ℝ) • ‖(x : SphereAmbient n)‖⁻¹ • (x : SphereAmbient n) = r x
    simp only [one_smul, r]

  exact hr'

                                          private theorem singleSphere_integration_by_parts {n : ℕ}
    (f : SpherePoint n → ℝ) (V : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n)
    (hf : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 f)
    (hV : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V)
    (hTangent : ∀ x : SpherePoint n, inner ℝ (x : SphereAmbient n) (V x) = 0) :
    Integrable (sphereTangentDivergence V) (sphereUniformMeasure n) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x) (sphereUniformMeasure n) ∧
    Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) (sphereUniformMeasure n) ∧
    (∫ x, sphereTangentDivergence V x ∂sphereUniformMeasure n) = 0 ∧
    (∫ x, f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x ∂sphereUniformMeasure n) =
      -(∫ x, inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x) ∂sphereUniformMeasure n) := by
  have hW : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 (fun x => f x • V x) := hf.smul hV
  have hWTangent (x : SpherePoint n) : inner ℝ (x : SphereAmbient n) (f x • V x) = 0 := by
    rw [inner_smul_right, hTangent x, mul_zero]
  have hmul : Continuous (fun x => f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x) :=
    hf.continuous.mul (continuous_tangentDivergence V hV)
  have hpair : Continuous (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) := by
    have heq : (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) =

      funext x
      rw [tangentDivergence_smul f V hf hV hTangent x]
      ring
    rw [heq]
    exact (continuous_tangentDivergence _ hW).sub hmul
  have hImul : Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereTangentDivergence V x) (sphereUniformMeasure n) := by
    simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using hmul.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
      (μ := sphereUniformMeasure n) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
  have hIpair : Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (sphereTangentGradient f x) (V x)) (sphereUniformMeasure n) := by
    simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using hpair.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
      (μ := sphereUniformMeasure n) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
  refine ⟨integrable_tangentDivergence V hV, hImul, hIpair,
    integral_tangentDivergence_eq_zero V hV hTangent, ?_⟩
  have hzero := integral_tangentDivergence_eq_zero (fun x => f x • V x) hW hWTangent
  simp_rw [tangentDivergence_smul f V hf hV hTangent] at hzero

                                          Download module (.lean)
                                          private theorem integral_configuration_divergence_coordinate_eq_zero {n N : ℕ}
    (V : SphereConfiguration n N → SphereAmbient n)
    (hV : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V)
    (i : Fin N)
    (hTangent : ∀ x : SphereConfiguration n N, inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (V x) = 0) :
    (∫ x, sphereTangentDivergence (fun z => V (Function.update x i z)) (x i)
      ∂sphereProductMeasure n N) = 0 := by
  cases N with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 i
  | succ N =>
    let σ := sphereUniformMeasure n
    let μ := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin N => σ)
    let H : SphereConfiguration n (N + 1) → ℝ := fun x =>
      sphereTangentDivergence (fun z => V (Function.update x i z)) (x i)
    have hI : Integrable H (sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) := by
      simpa only [integrableOn_univ] using
        (continuous_configuration_divergence_coordinate V hV i).continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
          (μ := sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) (K := Set.univ) isCompact_univ
    let e := MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ : Fin (N + 1) => SpherePoint n) i
    have hmp : MeasurePreserving e (sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) (σ.prod μ) :=
      measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => σ) i
    let q := H ∘ e.symm
    have hq : Integrable q (σ.prod μ) :=
      (hmp.symm.integrable_comp_emb e.symm.measurableEmbedding).mpr hI
    have hqval (y : SpherePoint n) (z : Fin N → SpherePoint n) : q (y, z) =
        sphereTangentDivergence (fun w => V (i.insertNth w z)) y := by
      change sphereTangentDivergence
        (fun w => V (Function.update (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z) i w)) ((i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z) i) = _
      simp only [Fin.insertNth_apply_same, Fin.update_insertNth]
    have hinner (z : Fin N → SpherePoint n) : (∫ y, q (y, z) ∂σ) = 0 := by
      let x0 : SpherePoint n := ⟨EuclideanSpace.single 0 (1 : ℝ), by simp⟩
      have hs : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) (sphereProductModel n (N + 1)) 1
          (fun y => i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z) := by
        have h := contMDiff_sphereSection 1 (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) x0 z) i
        simpa only [Fin.update_insertNth] using h
      have hW : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1
          (fun y => V (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z)) := hV.comp hs
      have hWT (y : SpherePoint n) : inner ℝ (y : SphereAmbient n) (V (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z)) = 0 := by
        simpa only [Fin.insertNth_apply_same] using hTangent (i.insertNth (α := fun _ => SpherePoint n) y z)
      simp_rw [hqval]
      exact integral_tangentDivergence_eq_zero _ hW hWT
    calc
      (∫ x, H x ∂sphereProductMeasure n (N + 1)) = ∫ z, q z ∂σ.prod μ :=
        (hmp.symm.integral_comp e.symm.measurableEmbedding H).symm
      _ = ∫ z, ∫ y, q (y, z) ∂σ ∂μ := integral_prod_symm q hq
      _ = 0 := by simp only [hinner, integral_zero]

                                          private theorem sphereProductDivergence_smul {n N : ℕ}
    (f : SphereConfiguration n N → ℝ)
    (V : Fin N → SphereConfiguration n N → SphereAmbient n)
    (hf : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 f)
    (hV : ∀ i, ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 (V i))
    (hTangent : ∀ (x : SphereConfiguration n N) (i : Fin N),

    (x : SphereConfiguration n N) :

      f x * sphereProductDivergence V x +
        ∑ i : Fin N, inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x) := by

      sphereTangentDivergence (fun z => f (Function.update x i z) • V i (Function.update x i z)) (x i) =
        f x * sphereTangentDivergence (fun z => V i (Function.update x i z)) (x i) +
          inner ℝ (sphereProductGradient f i x) (V i x) := by
    have hfs : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 (fun z => f (Function.update x i z)) :=
      hf.comp (contMDiff_sphereSection 1 x i)
    have hVs : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 (fun z => V i (Function.update x i z)) :=
      (hV i).comp (contMDiff_sphereSection 1 x i)

      simpa only [Function.update_self] using hTangent (Function.update x i z) i
    simpa only [Function.update_eq_self, sphereProductGradient] using
      tangentDivergence_smul _ _ hfs hVs hTs (x i)
  simp only [sphereProductDivergence]
  simp_rw [hcoord]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]

                                          private theorem radialExtension_actual_differential {n : ℕ} {A : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A]
    (f : SpherePoint n → A) (hf : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, A) 1 f)
    (x : SpherePoint n) :
    let D := fderiv ℝ (sphereRadialExtension f) (x : SphereAmbient n)
    let J := mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) x
    let P := (ℝ ∙ (x : SphereAmbient n))ᗮ.starProjection
    D (x : SphereAmbient n) = 0 ∧ D.comp J = mvfderiv (𝓡 n) f x ∧ D.comp P = D := by
  let : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ (SphereAmbient n) = n + 1) := ⟨by simp [SphereAmbient]⟩
  dsimp only
  let D := fderiv ℝ (sphereRadialExtension f) (x : SphereAmbient n)
  have hd := (contDiffAt_radialExtension f hf (ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere x)).differentiableAt one_ne_zero
  have hnormal : D (x : SphereAmbient n) = 0 := by
    let l : ℝ → SphereAmbient n := fun t => (1 + t) • (x : SphereAmbient n)
    have hl : HasDerivAt l (x : SphereAmbient n) 0 := by
      simpa [l] using (((hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).const_add 1).smul_const (x : SphereAmbient n))
    have hd' : DifferentiableAt ℝ (sphereRadialExtension f) (l 0) := by simpa [l] using hd
    have hpos : ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in 𝓝 0, 0 < 1 + t :=
      (isOpen_lt continuous_const (continuous_const.add continuous_id)).mem_nhds (by simp)
    have he : sphereRadialExtension f ∘ l =ᶠ[𝓝 0] fun _ => sphereRadialExtension f (x : SphereAmbient n) :=
      hpos.mono fun t ht => radialExtension_pos_smul f (x : SphereAmbient n) ht
    have hdv := hd'.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt 0 hl
    have hz := (hasDerivAt_const 0 (sphereRadialExtension f (x : SphereAmbient n))).congr_of_eventuallyEq he
    simpa [l, D] using hdv.unique hz
  have he : sphereRadialExtension f ∘ ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) = f :=
    funext (radialExtension_on_sphere f)
  have hco := (contMDiff_coe_sphere (n := n) (m := 1) x).mdifferentiableAt one_ne_zero
  have hchain : D.comp (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n) x) =
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) f x := by
    have hc := mfderiv_comp x hd.mdifferentiableAt hco
    rw [he, mfderiv_eq_fderiv] at hc
    exact hc.symm
  refine ⟨hnormal, hchain, ?_⟩
  ext v
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val,
    Submodule.starProjection_unit_singleton ℝ (norm_eq_of_mem_sphere x), map_sub, map_smul,
    hnormal, smul_zero, sub_zero]

    (V : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n)
    (hV : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V) (x : SpherePoint n) :

                                          private theorem tangentDivergence_eq_tangent_trace {n : ℕ}
    (V : SpherePoint n → SphereAmbient n)
    (hV : ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 V) (x : SpherePoint n) :
    let K := (ℝ ∙ (x : SphereAmbient n))ᗮ

                                          This is a static integration identity for the specified normalized polar measure and its finite product. It gives no derivative in time, entropy evolution, diffusion existence, or density PDE. Identifying another supplied measure, gradient, divergence, or model generator with these definitions is a separate application obligation. The proof derives the required radial regularity from the intrinsic hypotheses. It neither assumes nor asserts that the totalized radial extension is continuous or differentiable at the origin. All integrals are ordinary finite real integrals. The conclusions include integrability, and no almost-everywhere-in-time or finite-horizon convention is involved. The zero-dimensional sphere and empty product are included. The proof retains the radial factor \(r^n/r\) on positive radii; it does not replace the exponent by truncated natural subtraction. The stated regularity is classical C¹/C². No weak-gradient, Sobolev, nonsmooth-weight, or arbitrary-measure extension is claimed.

                                          Complete source statement and conditions

                                          For arbitrary \(n,N\in\mathbb N\), use \(E=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), its unit sphere \(S\), \(M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\), the induced product smooth and metric structures, and the exact normalized polar product measure \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\) defined below. For every real \(f,\rho\in C^1(M)\) and \(g\in C^2(M)\), define the actual tangent field \(V_i=\rho\nabla_i g\). Then the three displayed integrands are integrable, its divergence has zero integral, and the weighted integration-by-parts identity holds. The field regularity and tangency are derived from these hypotheses. The weight \(\rho\) has no sign or normalization restriction.

                                          • \(n,N\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary, with no positivity restriction. Thus the ambient dimension is \(n+1\); \(n=0\) gives the two-point sphere and \(N=0\) gives a one-point empty product.
                                          • The scalar field is \(\mathbb R\). All norms, inner products, tangent projections and manifold metrics are induced by the Euclidean structure. Regularity means regularity in the usual stereographic sphere charts and their finite product charts.
                                          • The reference measure is exactly \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\), with \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau\) and \(\tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere}\). Its finite nonzero mass and probability normalization are proved internally; they are not extra inputs.
                                          • For every \(f,\rho,g:M\to\mathbb R\), assume \(f,\rho\in C^1(M)\) and \(g\in C^2(M)\), jointly in all configuration coordinates.
                                          • The field is defined by \(V_i(x)=\rho(x)\nabla_i g(x)\). Its C¹ regularity and pointwise tangency are derived. No sign, strict positivity, normalization, or density interpretation is assumed for \(\rho\).

                                          Weighted gradient integration by parts on product spheres

                                          \[\begin{gathered}V_i=\rho\nabla_i g,\qquad\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad f\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad\rho\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,\nabla_i g\rangle\in L^1(\mu),\\\int_M\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=0,\\\int_Mf\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=-\int_M\rho\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,\nabla_i g\rangle\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]

                                          Samplinglib mathematical lesson

                                          Weighted gradient integration by parts on product spheres

                                          Read this first

                                          Mathematical statement

                                          For arbitrary \(n,N\in\mathbb N\), use \(E=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), its unit sphere \(S\), \(M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\), the induced product smooth and metric structures, and the exact normalized polar product measure \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\) defined below. For every real \(f,\rho\in C^1(M)\) and \(g\in C^2(M)\), define the actual tangent field \(V_i=\rho\nabla_i g\). Then the three displayed integrands are integrable, its divergence has zero integral, and the weighted integration-by-parts identity holds. The field regularity and tangency are derived from these hypotheses. The weight \(\rho\) has no sign or normalization restriction.

                                          \[\begin{gathered}V_i=\rho\nabla_i g,\qquad\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad f\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad\rho\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,\nabla_i g\rangle\in L^1(\mu),\\\int_M\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=0,\\\int_Mf\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=-\int_M\rho\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,\nabla_i g\rangle\,d\mu.\end{gathered}\]
                                          Lean statement · sphere_product_weighted_gradient_integration_by_parts

                                          The type quantifies n and N first, then f, rho and g. It assumes C¹ f, C¹ rho and C² g and defines V locally in the conclusion. It does not assume C¹ regularity or tangency of that derived field.
